title: Bakery Rush Order Profit
description:
## Task

A bakery takes rush orders. Each order needs exactly one hour of the single oven and pays a reward, but only if it is baked in an hour numbered from 1 up to its deadline (hour 1 is the first hour of the day). The oven bakes one order per hour. Choose which orders to bake, and in which hours, to maximise the total reward, and return that reward. With up to 10^5 orders and deadlines up to 10^9, an O(n^2) scheduling table or trying every subset is too slow.

## Input

- `orders` — a list of `[deadline, reward]` pairs of positive integers, in any order. It may be empty.

## Output

The largest total reward obtainable (an integer).

## Example

```python
best_rush_reward([[2, 100], [1, 19], [2, 27], [1, 25], [3, 15]])  # returns 142
best_rush_reward([[1, 5], [1, 9]])  # returns 9
best_rush_reward([])  # returns 0
```

## Constraints

- 0 ≤ number of orders ≤ 10^5
- 1 ≤ `deadline` ≤ 10^9
- 1 ≤ `reward` ≤ 10^9
